Undergraduate entry requirements
Equivalent regional qualifications for A-level requirements (these can be found on the undergraduate programme you intend to study):
Indian School Certificate (ISC/CISCE)
GCSE A or B: Grade X marks can be used
A*AA: Indian School Certificate Class XII (ISC) certificate overall score 85%
AAA: Indian School Certificate Class XII (ISC) certificate overall score 80%
AAB: Indian School Certificate Class XII (ISC) certificate overall score 75%
ABB: Indian School Certificate Class XII (ISC) certificate overall score 75%
BBB: Indian School Certificate Class XII (ISC) certificate overall score 75%
Intermediate Certificate (version of a State Board qualification)
A*AA: Intermediate Public Examination overall score 90%
AAA: Intermediate Public Examination overall score 85%
AAB: Intermediate Public Examination overall score 80%
ABB: Intermediate Public Examination overall score 80%
BBB: Intermediate Public Examination overall score 75%
Higher School Certificate (version of a State Board qualification)
GCSE A or B: State Board Grade X marks can be used
A*AA: State Board High School Certificate overall score 90%
AAA: State Board High school Certificate overall score 85%
AAB: State Board High School Certificate overall score 80%
ABB: State Board High School Certificate overall score 80%
BBB: State Board High School Certificate overall score 75%
Higher Secondary Certificate (version of a State Board qualification)
GCSE A or B: State Board Grade X marks can be used
All India Senior School Certificate (CBSE)
A*AA: All India Senior Secondary School Year 12 certificate overall score 85%
AAA: All India Senior Secondary School Year 12 certificate overall score 80%
AAB: All India Senior Secondary School Year 12 certificate overall score 75%
ABB: All India Senior Secondary School Year 12 certificate overall score 75%

Postgraduate taught entry requirements
We normally accept a Bachelor degree with the following grade equivalencies:
For programmes requiring a UK 2.1 Honours degree: Bachelor degree with 55-63% (depending on university attended)
For programmes requiring a UK 2.2 Honours degree: Bachelor degree with 50-58% (depending on university attended)

Prospective Student Information Sessions
The University of Glasgow is pleased to invite all prospective students to online information sessions which will be dedicated to answering your questions about joining #TeamUofG.
The team will give a presentation covering the application process, entry requirements and student life. There will be time at the end of the presentation for you to ask questions.
Click the relevant link below to book your place.

If you want to come to Glasgow for a year abroad and your country does not have an existing agreement please look at our incoming Study Abroad Programme options
Meet Us
Students who choose to be counselled by an agency should expect the following standards of service:
Representatives will support students throughout the application process, providing advice and assistance in the preparation/submission of documents. It is, however, the applicant who must remain ultimately responsible for their account and the management of communications.
Representatives will have full access to student data contained within the application form and may manage a student application by discussing all aspects of the application with the University of Glasgow.
Representatives should be honest and accurate in communicating information about the University to the student and vice versa. At no time should representatives disseminate false or misleading information to the student or to the University.
Representatives will conduct themselves with fairness and integrity at all times and are subject to a rigorous selection and ongoing training process by the University of Glasgow.
Representatives are paid by the University for their services and will not pass on charges to prospective students.

Get to Know Glasgow podcast: India episode
In this special bonus episode of our Get to Know Glasgow podcast, watch Indian students Navya (undergraduate), Riddhi and Rohit (both postgraduate) share their experiences of studying at the University of Glasgow, hosted by Maneeta from our in-country team in India.

More about the podcast
In each episode, you’ll learn about student life in Glasgow from the people who know it best: real UofG students. They share their experiences and top tips on everything from accommodation to scholarships to the cost of living.
Press play to listen to this ‘Student Employability’ episode, with Indian student Ash sharing his experiences of finding work and employment opportunities in Glasgow.
